correctness.rationale: The exact distance-two visibility predicate is proved by enumerating the two geodesic midpoints for each pair. Translation at any distance-two pair gives an exhaustive list of allowed words, whose weight-two supports form an intersecting-edge family. A star implies containment in a radius-one ball, and the only non-star family is a triangle, giving exactly one affine parity tetrahedron. A selected pair of midpoints is explicitly excluded. Both types satisfy visibility; no tetrahedron lies in any ball, while distinct balls overlap in at most two vertices. These lemmas justify unique counting for subsets of size at least three, exact tetrahedron multiplicity \(2^{d-2}\binom d3\), and facet exhaustiveness. Independent brute-path enumerations cover 256+65536+1149017=1214809 subsets in dimensions three through five; finite tests do not establish infinite scope.

value.rationale: The result completely enumerates a natural new distance-limited visibility family on all labeled binary cubes, not just the maximum size. Its non-obvious four-point parity-tetrahedron orbit contributes an explicit correction beyond the union of ball simplices. The resulting facet census determines every maximal configuration and shows sharply nonpure behavior in every \(d\ge4\), with minimum maximal size four versus maximum d+1. These are motivated structural/quantitative invariants of the same graph problem and are not obtained from the previously published µ2 equality. The contribution does not rely on an arbitrary finite parameter slice; finite verifier dimensions are auxiliary.
